conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ve reviewed your chart and wanted to talk about why you came in today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, yes. I’ve had this cough and low fevers for about a week now. Started with a sore throat and congestion.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And your husband was sick recently too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, he had flu-like symptoms. I thought I’d get better, but the cough just stuck around.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. We tested you in the ER and found you have RSV — that’s a respiratory virus, common in adults but can be more serious in people with weakened immunity.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Is that dangerous for me?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Because of your history — the stem cell transplant and ongoing immune suppression — we take it seriously. But you’re not having trouble breathing, and your oxygen level is good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I did notice some wheezing at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we heard that. We gave you an albuterol treatment, and your lungs are sounding much clearer now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I use my inhaler at home sometimes, especially when I feel tight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep that available for you here and send it home with instructions to use as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also did a chest X-ray to make sure there’s no pneumonia. Good news — your lungs look clear.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. I was worried about that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also checked your flu swab — it was negative — and no bacteria in blood or urine. So RSV is the main issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my immune system? I get IVIG every week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re going to give you your scheduled IVIG infusion tomorrow. It’ll help support your immunity while you fight this virus.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes me feel better. What about my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re continuing your regular medications — prednisone for GVHD, antivirals, antifungals, and your blood thinner.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One change — we lowered your long-acting morphine dose. It can slow stomach emptying, which might worsen bloating or diarrhea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, right. I’ve had that problem before. I’ve been using loperamide and stool softeners.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and you’re reporting regular bowel movements now, which is great. We’ll keep those on board as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My back’s been a little stiff, but not worse than usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We see you have osteoporosis and old compression fractures. You’re on baclofen and vitamin D — we’ll keep that up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my liver enzymes — they’ve been a bit high before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your liver tests are mildly elevated, which we expect with chronic GVHD. But your recent biopsy didn’t show active GVH in the liver.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So we’re not changing anything there?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we’ll keep your prednisone at 7.5 mg daily and continue the eye drops for dry eyes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Morning. My cough is a bit better, and I haven’t wheezed since yesterday’s treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re going to give your IVIG infusion later this morning — same dose you get weekly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any other blood tests today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your labs this morning. White count went up a bit, which is expected with infection. Liver enzymes are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my kidney function? Glucose was high last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your kidney function is fine. Glucose was a bit high, but likely from the stress of illness. We didn’t see signs of diabetes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. You got your IVIG a little while ago. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m okay. A little tired, but no headache or reaction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. That means it went smoothly. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow morning if you keep improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Any follow-up I should know about?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes — plan to see your hematologist in two weeks. And your next IVIG is in about a month, unless you have issues before then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re looking well. We’re going to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. Is everything in order?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your cough is much better, lungs are clear, and you’re back to your baseline. We’ll send you home with instructions and a full med list.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I watch for anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call if you develop fever, shortness of breath, or worsening cough. Otherwise, keep using your albuterol if you wheeze.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other symptoms — joint pain, stomach — should stay the same?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, those are managed as before. Continue your GVHD and pain meds, and the lovenox for blood clot prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and don’t hesitate to call if anything comes up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. The nurse will go over discharge papers shortly.
